title: VSift JSONL progress event v1
description: How far a long operation has come, in an --events jsonl stream (P11, ADR 0021): transcript.retranscribe and job.resume (chunks recognised, reused chunks included) the worker commands job.run and job.batch, and setup.install (fetching_artifact: bytes of the artifact being downloaded or imported; installing_components: components of the accepted plan finished). Advisory: at most one per second and 4,096 per request; an update inside the second replaces the pending one, and a host drops progress rather than block on a slow reader, counting the drops in progress_dropped (for this request, before this event). The terminal event stays authoritative. operation_id is null (the command's operation id is in the terminal event); request_operation_id names the worker request, null for other commands; job_id names the recoverable job, when the work runs as one. Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033) a recognising_speech event also carries media, how far the recognition has come in media time, with its speed and estimate ($defs.media_progress, the same definition as job-data.schema.json's, held equal by a contract test); job.start reports progress too. Every line is at most 64 KiB.

media_progress.description: How far a recognition has come in media time (ADR 0033): done_us of total_us microseconds of the recording (total_us null when the end is not known), elapsed_ms of wall time in this attempt, speed in media seconds a wall second over the chunks recognised in this attempt (null before the first; chunks reused from checkpoints do not count), percent done rounded down (null without an end), and estimate, the wall time left as the media still to do over that speed (basis cumulative_measured_speed), null until at least two fresh chunks and 20 s of work have run, and in job.status only while a process runs the stream. Advisory: optimistic over silence.
